entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 12_Victoria_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 1434 vertices and 2864 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 116 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (177°, -27°), period 8.660345 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 57.83584545124532 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: The live source folder https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/12Victoria/ contains Deconv/ and Red/. Reduced and deconvolved observations therefore have a concrete archive route. Their pixels, image geometry, coverage and photometry were not qualified in this directory-level check, so these files cannot yet be treated as a registered global reflectance map. The current grid remains an explicit missing-imagery presentation.
entries.revisitWhen: The original image headers and publication establish a usable projection onto this specific MPCD model, and a native-pixel comparison qualifies geometry, illumination and measured coverage.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 12_Victoria_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation or scientific comparison specifically requires this alternative mesh and its matching source frame.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Corrected: DAMIT does list models for this body, 1840 (quality 4, nonconvex) and 844, whose pole matches the survey's published one within a degree, so the column order was never the blocker. The blocker is the archive: 12_Victoria_param.txt and 12_Victoria_adam.obj are both listed in the release directory but answer 403, while the MPCD mesh and all 20 deconvolved frames are served. Measured with DAMIT model 1840's IAU spin record on the MPCD mesh, the outline places the body 13.61 degrees off over 12 of 20 scored frames against a 2.86-degree floor; sweeping the prime meridian freely, which would be circular, still leaves 5.34 degrees at best. Of the whole survey list this body's outline is the most registrable, 71 percent of rotation phases above the rule's threshold, so it is worth reopening if those two files ever answer. Measured outside preparation by the registration stage's own modules (its limb fit, camera and caliper rule) driven from the pinned inputs, which reproduces Sylvia's prepared report to the digit (15 scored, rms 2.887, floor 1.871, systematic 2.198); on Themis it read 2.92 degrees where the stage itself read 1.65, so treat these as the rule applied to the frames, not as a prepared verdict.
entries.revisitWhen: 12_Victoria_param.txt or 12_Victoria_adam.obj answering from the release directory, which would supply the frame the survey's own rotation record describes.
